TITLE: Evaluating Long-Horizon Web-Based Data Science Workflows with Financial Dataset Analysis
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of two state-of-the-art web agents (LLaMA and PaLM-2) on a real-world financial dataset (e.g., stock prices, earnings reports) obtained from various websites, using a custom dataset synthesis pipeline. The agents will be tasked with navigating to websites, downloading and preprocessing data, and generating insights such as trend analysis and predictions. We will evaluate the performance using a combination of metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score) for the generated insights, as well as a novel multi-step action evaluation metric that assesses the sequence of actions taken by the agents.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparison with a state-of-the-art data science library (e.g., Pandas, NumPy) applied to the same dataset, to demonstrate the superiority of the web-based approach. Additional controls include varying the complexity of the financial dataset and the websites used to obtain it.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvements in accuracy and insight generation when using the web agents compared to the traditional data science library, but may struggle with complex financial datasets that require domain-specific knowledge.

The synthesis pipeline will be designed to mirror real-world financial data collection and processing pipelines, and will include data augmentation and_noise injection to simulate real-world variability. The multi-step action evaluation metric will be designed to capture the sequence of actions taken by the agents, including successful and unsuccessful actions, as well as corrections and retries. This metric will provide a more nuanced understanding of the agents' performance and their ability to navigate complex data science workflows.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Robustness of Web Agents to Changing Website Structure
PROPOSAL: Develop a dynamic webpage generation system that periodically updates the structure and content of a set of websites used for training and evaluation. This system will generate new versions of websites with varying degrees of changes, such as new navigation menus, added or removed content, and changed layout. We will then train a state-of-the-art web agent (e.g., DALL-E 3.5B) on these changing websites and evaluate its performance on a set of tasks (e.g., finding specific information, extracting data) with varying levels of similarity to the training data.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the web agent trained on the changing websites to one trained on a static version of the same websites, as well as to a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the web agent trained on the changing websites to outperform the baseline model, but may struggle with abrupt changes in website structure that require significant retraining to adapt.

This proposal will help assess the long-term robustness of web agents, which is crucial for real-world applications where websites are frequently updated. The dynamic webpage generation system will provide a flexible and realistic testing environment for web agents, allowing us to evaluate their adaptability to changing website structures and content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Taskonomy for Web-Based Data Science: A Hierarchical Framework for Action Clustering
PROPOSAL: Design a taskonomy for web-based data science, where a set of web-based data science tasks are hierarchically clustered into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) based on their complexity and Granularity. This framework will provide a shared vocabulary for action clustering and facilitate the development of web agents capable of adapting to different tasks and datasets. We will apply this framework to real-world datasets and evaluate the performance of a state-of-the-art web agent (e.g., LLaMA) on the resulting clusters.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the web agent on taskonomies generated using different clustering algorithms (e.g., k-means, DBSCAN) and with a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the taskonomy framework to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of web agents, allowing them to adapt to new tasks and datasets with minimal retraining. However, the success of the framework may depend on the quality of the initial clustering and the selection of relevant features for action clustering.

This proposal will provide a fundamental shift in the way we approach web-based data science, enabling the development of more flexible and adaptable web agents. The taskonomy framework will allow us to semantically organize web-based data science tasks, facilitating the creation of domain-agnostic web agents that can generalize across different tasks and datasets.

ACTION: REVISION
TITLE: Taskonomy for Web-Based Data Science: A Hierarchical Framework for Action Clustering
PROPOSAL: REVISION: Include an expert-in-the-loop evaluation phase, where domain experts provide feedback on the quality and relevance of the action clusters generated by the taskonomy framework. This phase will help refine the taskonomy and enable the web agent to adapt to new tasks and datasets more effectively.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the web agent on taskonomies generated with and without expert feedback, as well as with a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 10 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the taskonomy framework with expert feedback to further improve the efficiency and effectiveness of web agents, allowing them to adapt to new tasks and datasets with high accuracy.

The expert-in-the-loop evaluation phase will provide a crucial step towards developing more accurate and relevant action clusters for web-based data science tasks. By incorporating domain expert feedback, we can improve the reliability and adaptability of the web agent, enabling it to generalize more effectively across different tasks and datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding Agent Failure Modes in Web-Based Data Science Workflows
PROPOSAL: Design a framework to systematically identify and quantify failure modes in web-based data science workflows, with a focus on understanding the underlying causes of these failures. We will develop a set of canonical failure modes and survey a range of web agents on a suite of tasks, with the goal of identifying common failure patterns and developing strategies for mitigating them.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of web agents on tasks with and without canonical failure modes, as well as with a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to identify a small set of common failure modes that affect a large proportion of web agents, and to develop effective strategies for mitigating these failures.

This proposal will provide a fundamental understanding of the failure modes that plague web-based data science workflows, and will enable the development of more robust and reliable web agents. By systematically identifying and quantifying failure modes, we can develop targeted strategies for improving web agent performance and reliability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human-AI Collaboration for Web-Based Data Science Workflows
PROPOSAL: Develop a human-AI collaboration framework for web-based data science workflows, where a web agent is paired with a human collaborator to jointly complete complex tasks. We will design a system to facilitate communication and collaboration between the web agent and human, and evaluate the benefits of human-AI collaboration on task completion time, accuracy, and user satisfaction.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of human-AI collaboration to solo human completion of tasks, as well as to a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (plus additional computational resources for human collaboration)
PREDICTION: We expect human-AI collaboration to significantly improve task completion time, accuracy, and user satisfaction, by leveraging the strengths of both humans and AI in web-based data science workflows.

This proposal will explore the potential of human-AI collaboration to revolutionize web-based data science workflows. By combining the strengths of humans and AI, we can create more efficient, accurate, and user-friendly systems for complex data science tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Explainability of Web Agent Decisions in Data Science Workflows
PROPOSAL: Develop a framework to evaluate the explainability of web agent decisions in data science workflows, by analyzing the reasoning process of the web agent and the relationships between its actions and decisions. We will design a set of metrics and techniques to quantify the explainability of web agent decisions, and apply these metrics to a range of web agents and data science tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the explainability of web agent decisions to those of a human expert in data science, as well as to a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the explainability framework to significantly improve our understanding of web agent decision-making processes, and to provide insights for improving the transparency and trustworthiness of web agents in data science workflows.

This proposal will focus on the critical issue of explainability in web agent decision-making, which is crucial for building trust and ensuring transparency in AI-driven data science workflows. By developing a framework to evaluate and quantify the explainability of web agent decisions, we can identify opportunities for improvement and optimize the decision-making processes of web agents.

TITLE: Assessing the Generalizability of Web Agents across Different Domains and Tasks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the generalizability of web agents across different domains and tasks, by training and testing web agents on a diverse set of datasets and tasks, and analyzing their performance and adaptability in new contexts. We will also investigate the transferability of knowledge and representations learned by web agents in one domain to others.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of web agents trained on a specific domain or task to those trained on a diversified set of domains and tasks, as well as to a baseline model that relies on pre-computed webpage features.
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the web agents trained on a diversified set of domains and tasks to show improved generalizability and adaptability across new contexts, but may struggle with tasks that require significant domain expertise.

This proposal will focus on the critical issue of generalizability in web agents, which is crucial for building AI systems that can adapt to new and dynamic domains. By evaluating the generalizability of web agents across different domains and tasks, we can identify opportunities for improvement and develop more robust and adaptable web agents.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Web-Based Data Science Benchmark Suite for Evaluating Web Agents
PROPOSAL: Design and develop a comprehensive benchmark suite for evaluating web agents in web-based data science workflows, including a diverse set of tasks, datasets, and metrics for measuring agent performance. We will also establish a shared evaluation platform for the web agent community to compare and validate their models.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of state-of-the-art web agents on the benchmark suite to a set of baseline models, as well as to a human expert in data science.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the benchmark suite to become a standard evaluation platform for web agents in web-based data science workflows, enabling better sharing of knowledge, comparison of methods, and continuous improvement of agent performance.

This proposal will focus on the critical issue of evaluating web agents in web-based data science workflows, which is essential for advancing the field of web-based AI. By developing a comprehensive benchmark suite, we can establish a baseline for measuring agent performance, facilitate collaboration and knowledge-sharing among research teams, and promote the development of more effective web agents.

TITLE: Large-Scale Deployment and Integration of Web Agents in Real-World Data Science Workflows
PROPOSAL: Collaborate with industry partners to integrate and deploy web agents into real-world data science workflows, tackling challenging data science tasks and showcasing the benefits of web-based AI. We will also investigate the challenges and opportunities of scaling web agents to meet the demands of complex, real-world data science workflows.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of web agents in real-world deployment to those in controlled laboratory settings, as well as to traditional data science approaches.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (plus additional resources for collaboration and deployment)
PREDICTION: We expect the large-scale deployment and integration of web agents to demonstrate significant benefits in terms of efficiency, accuracy, and scalability, and to showcase the potential of web-based AI in real-world data science applications.

This proposal will focus on the practical applications of web agents in real-world data science workflows, building on the foundations established by our previous proposals. By deploying web agents in real-world settings, we can demonstrate their effectiveness, identify challenges and opportunities for improvement, and push the boundaries of what is possible with web-based AI.

TITLE: Web-Based Data Science Agent Evaluator: Task Definition
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive evaluation framework for web-based data science agents, comprising a diverse set of scenarios that simulate real-world web-based data science workflows. Specifically, the framework will include the following tasks:
- Data acquisition through web navigation (e.g., extracting data from websites related to economic and financial indicators, public health data, or demographic trends)
- Data cleaning and pre-processing (e.g., removing duplicates, handling missing values)
- Data analysis (e.g., statistical inference, forecasting, text analysis)
- Insight generation (e.g., identifying trends, patterns, or correlations)
- Downstream actions (e.g., generating reports, visualizations, or creating executive summaries)
Each task will be designed to evaluate specific aspects of agent performance, such as robustness, adaptability, or ability to generalize.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art web navigation agents (e.g., LLaMA, Maha, radar), which will serve as baselines for comparison.
COST: Estimated 100 GPU-hours (comprising pre-processing, model training, and evaluation).
PREDICTION: Agents will perform remarkably well on some tasks but struggle with data cleaning and pre-processing, showcasing a significant gap between current capabilities and realistic data science workflows.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Specific Evaluation Metrics
PROPOSAL: Introduce a set of fine-grained evaluation metrics tailored to each task in the web-based data science workflow. These metrics will capture the nuanced aspects of agent performance and enable comprehensive scoring of complex, multi-step outputs. Some proposed metrics include:
- Precision/recall/F1 scores for data cleaning and pre-processing tasks
- Mean absolute error or mean squared error for predictive tasks (e.g., forecasting)
- ROUGE or BLEU scores for text-based outputs (e.g., summarization)
- Visual metrics for quality and interpretability of generated visualizations
- Novelty or creativity metrics to encourage innovative insights
These metrics will be employed in conjunction with existing evaluation frameworks to provide a more comprehensive understanding of agent strengths and weaknesses.
CONTROLS: Existing metrics from the state-of-the-art web navigation agents (e.g., click-through rates, success rates) and the comprehensive framework proposed in Task Definition (1).
COST: Estimated 50 GPU-hours (focusing on developing and refining these metrics).
PREDICTION: Agents will exhibit significant performance variability across tasks, with some tasks demonstrating strong modeling capabilities but struggling with uncertainty or outliers.

TITLE: Real-World Data Collection and Curation
PROPOSAL: Gather and curate a diverse set of real-world datasets from various domains, including economic and financial data analysis, public health data analysis, demographics and public policy data, e-commerce and online forums, music metadata, and scientific literature metadata. These datasets will be used to evaluate the web-based data science agents' ability to handle real-world complexities and nuances. The datasets will be curated to ensure they cover a range of structures, sizes, and formats.
CONTROLS: Existing datasets will be used as a starting point, and new datasets will be collected and validated through a combination of human evaluation and automated checks.
COST: Estimated 200 GPU-hours (data curation, annotation, and pre-processing).
PREDICTION: The use of real-world datasets will reveal weaknesses in current agents' ability to handle data quality issues, missing values, and inconsistent formatting, highlighting the need for more robust data cleaning and pre-processing techniques.

PROPOSAL: Enhance the real-world data collection and curation process by incorporating the following:
- Additional data sources from emerging domains (e.g., social media, online reviews, customer feedback)
- More stringent data quality and annotations to ensure accurate and consistent evaluation of agent performance
- Integration of data from multiple websites, online repositories, and APIs to simulate real-world data heterogeneity
CONTROLS: Existing datasets and data collection pipelines will be adapted to accommodate these enhancements.
COST: Estimated 250 GPU-hours (expansion of data collection, quality control, and curation efforts).
PREDICTION: The enhanced dataset will provide a more comprehensive and challenging evaluation environment for web-based data science agents, highlighting strengths and weaknesses in their ability to handle complex, real-world data and identify areas for improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Agent Augmentation and Initialization
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of agent augmentation and initialization on their ability to complete web-based data science tasks. Agent augmentation will involve adding domain-specific knowledge or task-specific components to the agent, while initialization will focus on pre-training the agent on large datasets or fine-tuning it on smaller, task-specific datasets.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art web navigation agents (e.g., LLaMA, Maha, radar) will be used as baselines, and the effects of augmentation and initialization will be compared across different domains and tasks.
COST: Estimated 300 GPU-hours (training, testing, and evaluation of augmented and initialized agents).
PREDICTION: The results will show that agent augmentation can significantly enhance performance on specific tasks, especially those requiring domain expertise, while initialization can improve performance on tasks with a strong learned prior, but may degrade performance when agents are poorly adapted to the task at hand.

TITLE: Multi-Agent Framework and Competition
PROPOSAL: Develop a multi-agent framework where multiple web-based data science agents are tasked with completing the same set of web-based data science tasks. This framework will enable the evaluation of agent ensemble performance, identify areas of expertise, and foster competition among agents to improve overall performance.
CONTROLS: The comprehensive framework proposed in Task Definition (1) and the curated dataset developed in Real-World Data Collection and Curation (3) will be used to evaluate agent ensemble performance.
COST: Estimated 350 GPU-hours (training, testing, and evaluation of multi-agent frameworks and ensembles).
PREDICTION: The multi-agent competition will reveal significant performance gains through ensemble methods, with some agents showing expertise in specific domains or tasks, and others providing robustness and adaptability to the ensemble's overall performance.

PROPOSAL: Design and develop a user interface that enables seamless human-AI collaboration for web-based data science tasks. This interface will allow users to interact with and guide the agents, providing contextual information, and receiving explanations and insights from the agents.
CONTROLS: The agent augmentation and initialization methods developed in Agent Augmentation and Initialization (4) and the multi-agent framework in Multi-Agent Framework and Competition (5) will be integrated into the human-AI collaboration interface.
COST: Estimated 400 GPU-hours (development and testing of the human-AI collaboration interface).
PREDICTION: The human-AI collaboration interface will enable significant improvements in agent performance and user experience, as users can provide contextual information and receive actionable insights from the agents, ultimately leading to more efficient and effective completion of web-based data science tasks.

PROPOSAL: Deploy the developed web-based data science agent evaluator and human-AI collaboration interface in real-world settings, such as a cloud-based platform or a dedicated lab, and evaluate their effectiveness in real-world scenarios.
